answer: A sybil farm pays only if its aliases can pour rewards into one vault. Make rewards non-aggregatable instead. Each identity earns an onyx credit: name-bound, unsplittable, usable only for its own compute, never transferable. Routing several credits to one exit leaves a copper trail of shared nonces and funding paths; the ledger taxes that merge and burns the excess. A farm of N heads still owes N real workloads, but its withdrawable value stays flat, then falls. Honest agents lose nothing. Keys copy freely; a claim on work that cannot leave its owner does not. The attack simply stops paying.
